name: Example Biomaterial Progressive Disclosure Scenario
theory_seed: Can a bio-inspired hierarchical polymer composite improve toughness and fatigue resistance under cyclic loading?
evaluation_goal: Evaluate whether a theory agent can generate and revise scientific claims as biomaterial evidence is progressively disclosed.

isBasedOn.name: ProjectionBench: Evaluating Scientific Hypothesis Generation in LLMs Under Progressive Information Disclosure

disclosure_stages.name: Topic and research question
disclosure_stages.content: A polymer composite is inspired by biological hierarchical structures. The research question asks whether hierarchy can improve toughness and fatigue resistance.

disclosure_stages.name: Background disclosure
disclosure_stages.content: Hierarchical materials distribute stress across multiple length scales. Interfaces can deflect cracks and dissipate energy during deformation.

disclosure_stages.name: Methods disclosure
disclosure_stages.content: The composite is fabricated with aligned nanoscale reinforcement and microscale layered architecture. Cyclic loading tests measure fatigue resistance and crack propagation.

disclosure_stages.name: Results disclosure
disclosure_stages.content: Results show improved toughness, slower crack propagation, and higher fatigue resistance compared with a non-hierarchical polymer control.

reference_claims.claimReviewed: Hierarchical structure improves toughness in the polymer composite.
Interfaces deflect cracks and dissipate energy during deformation.
The hierarchical composite slows crack propagation under cyclic loading.
The hierarchical composite has higher fatigue resistance than a non-hierarchical polymer control.
